title: Signal Detection Theory for Feature Detection Sensitivity

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Rigorously characterizing SAE feature reliability is a methodological improvement. Separating sensitivity from bias is valuable for feature quality assessment. Safety connection is indirect -- better features enable better safety analysis.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: d-prime and ROC curves are standard statistics. SAELens provides activation distributions. The main challenge is obtaining ground-truth labels for concept presence, which requires manual annotation. Otherwise straightforward.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Hand-labeling ground truth for concept presence on enough examples to compute meaningful d-prime is time-consuming. For 5-10 features with 100+ examples each, annotation takes significant time. Feasible if scoped to 5 features.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
